Subject: LunaTech benchmarking runbook & onboarding handoff — throughput/latency gates

Hi Carlos,

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, I’ve pulled together a concise runbook for the onboarding benchmark so we can get to acceptance quickly. High-level ask: confirm the test window and the sample credentials, and sign off on the acceptance gates below. Once you confirm we’ll schedule the first run and share live telemetry.

Key objectives
- Verify 95th-percentile generation latency <= 220ms at 1k req/s steady-state for the 2048-token profile.
- Validate sustained throughput of 1,000–1,200 requests/sec (RLU-style workload) for 30 minutes.
- Validate KV/prefix caching effectiveness on typical session traffic.
- Capture traces and token-level cost estimate for the run.

Planned test profile (summary)
- Ramp: 0 -> 600rps over 5m, then -> 1,000rps over 3m.
- Sustain: 30m at target.
- Spike test: 3x traffic for 90s to observe graceful degradation.
- Payload mix: 75% short prompts (~64 tokens), 25% long prompts (~1,200 tokens) — see attached samples.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- P95 latency < 220ms for the short prompt mix at the target throughput.
- Error rate < 1% (5xx/timeout).
- Token cost per 1k responses <= agreed budget (we'll produce cost summary).

Artifacts we’ll produce
- Raw load-engine CSV (Locust) + aggregated P50/P95/P99.
- Prometheus + Jaeger traces for 1–2 failing flows.
- Post-run checklist + remediation recommendations (if gates not met).

Attachments included with this message: lunatech_api_samples.json (example requests). The full runbook and scripts live at the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedRunbook

Proposed windows (PST) — please pick one:
- Tue Jun 15, 10:00–11:30 (warm-up + 30m sustain + cool-down)
- Wed Jun 16, 03:00–04:30 (off-hours for higher capacity)

Operational asks from LunaTech
- API endpoint and API key with test scope (short-lived).
- Any rate-limiting gateways or egress NAT IPs to whitelist.
- Contact for network troubleshooting (on-call).

If you’re good with this, please reply with the preferred window and attach the test credentials. We’ll loop in CS and infra on our side (Dev and Vanessa on cc).

Thanks,

--
Tessa Morgan

Thanks Carlos/Tessa — I’ll own the run execution and the telemetry collection. Quick technical notes and the updated test script attached (lt_locust_plan.py):

Adjusted test details (engineer notes)
- Simulated RTT: we’ll add a 12–40ms tail latency jitter to mimic your customer paths.
- Concurrency model: 600 workers with per-worker pacing tuned to reach 1,100rps during sustain.
- Token accounting: we’ll record tokens-in/tokens-out per request and compute per-1k-response cost.
- KV caching test: run the 30m sustain twice — first cold cache, then warm cache immediately after to measure delta.

Observability hooks
- Prometheus scrape + Grafana dashboard (links in Drive).
- Jaeger tracing for 1% sampling; if we cross error-rate threshold we will increase to 10% for deeper traces.

Fallbacks & rollback
- If P95 > 300ms at target, auto-fallback to the smaller model variant (quantized) for the remainder of the window and we’ll mark run as degraded.
- If errors > 3% sustained for >2 min we will abort and produce a labeled run artifact.

I’ve attached lt_locust_plan.py and will commit the run config to the shared Drive before 09:00 PST.

—Dev

Team — quick notes from today’s run (initial observations):

- Run window executed at 10:00–11:10 PST (we shortened cool-down by 10m per customer request).
- Sustained target: 1,050rps for 30m (mix as planned).
- Initial aggregated numbers (preliminary): P95_short = 205ms, P99_short = 380ms, error rate = 0.9%. Cold vs warm cache showed ~28% P95 improvement.

Artifacts produced and next actions
- Attached: run-results-20270615.csv (raw durations + status codes).
- Drive folder updated with full Prometheus/Jaeger capture and our annotated runbook. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSharedRunbook
- Next steps: I’ll coordinate a 30-min postmortem with LunaTech this Friday to walk the traces and cost numbers; propose Fri Jun 18, 11:00 PST.

If anyone on our side can prep the cost-per-1k worksheet and the candidate quantized-model tradeoffs, please flag it here. We’ll need the materials for the postmortem and for the decision on SLA acceptance.

Thanks everyone — great run and smooth collaboration.
